{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The core risk-allocation provisions are strong and require no redline: Vendor's IP and operational indemnities (§ 20), ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables (§ 14, with the § 13.2 perpetual licence), the mutual liability cap with meaningful Excluded Claims (§ 21), our unrestricted assignment and change-of-control protections (§ 24), the subscription and paid-up licence grants (§ 13), New York law and venue (§ 28), the absence of minimum commitments (§ 2.1), post-termination transition and data return (§ 11), and Vendor insurance (§ 18).

Seven items require negotiation. Six are one-sided obligations running against us or gaps in our exit rights, and each fails the applicable fallback on a material term: exclusivity for the full term (§ 2.2), a Customer-payable daily liquidated damages penalty (§ 7.6), a Customer-side most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), the absence of any termination-for-convenience right against a three-year auto-renewing term (§ 9), unlimited unannounced Vendor audits with remote system access (§ 22.1), and a one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-hire (§ 12.4). Notably, §§ 2.1 and 12.3 already record that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, so several of these clauses conflict with the Agreement's own terms and deletion is the cleanest fix.

One item — the performance warranty (§ 19) — is marked **needs review**: the substantive analysis reads as compliant at the preferred position, but automated verification did not pass, so we are not stating a conclusion until the warranty period and remedy language are confirmed by manual read.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 21.3) | Full Vendor IP defence/indemnity; indemnities are Excluded Claims, so uncapped — better than fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with §§ 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) | Customer owns data and Deliverables; perpetual paid-up licence to embedded Vendor Technology. Draft Order Forms to capture all bespoke work product (§ 1.4). |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; robust Excluded Claims. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors; Vendor restricted; no change-of-control termination or repricing. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Full-term sole-and-exclusive provider commitment, no category limit, no performance exit — walk-away; conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day for "any delay in providing a dependency"; no cap, no materiality threshold — walk-away. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.4) | Licence extends to Affiliates and contractors; no at-will revocation. |
| High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended MFN running against us; no product, time or comparison limits — walk-away; conflicts with § 12.3. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to operate — retain. |
| High | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 | 180-day non-renewal notice is double the 90-day walk-away threshold; pricing limb (§ 8.3, lesser of CPI/3%) is compliant. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 | No Customer convenience right against a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals (§ 8.1–8.2) — walk-away. Vendor has none either. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote access to our systems — walk-away; contradicts § 22.2. Cost (§ 22.2) and confidentiality (§ 22.3) are compliant. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) | New York law and exclusive New York County venue; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with §§ 7.1, 12.3) | No minimum quantity, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way 18-month no-solicit/no-engage covering any Vendor employee, no carve-outs; no-hire element edges into walk-away; conflicts with § 12.3. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3, 10.1–10.2) | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; data return in 30 days; deletion only after confirmed return. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review** | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | Substantive read is compliant at the preferred position (90-day Deliverable period from later of delivery or acceptance; Services conform throughout the term), but verification did not pass. Confirm manually before we close this item. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, EL 1M for term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following clauses sit in walk-away territory or fail the fallback on a material term and cannot be accepted as drafted:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity.** Full-term exclusivity for the whole hosted analytics services line, with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no service-level or delivery-failure exit. We propose deletion; if exclusivity is commercially necessary, the fallback is a defined category, 12 months, and automatic termination on missed service levels.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, uncapped and with no materiality threshold; the § 21.1 mutual cap does not cure exposure that can still reach 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000. We propose deleting the LD and substituting an equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as its sole remedy; at most we would consider a single amount capped at three months' fees.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended obligation to extend Vendor our best supplier terms, with no defined product, time limit or comparison carve-outs. We propose deletion, consistent with § 12.3.
4. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Double the 90-day walk-away threshold and well beyond the 60-day fallback maximum. We propose 30 days plus a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal; 60 days is available as a fallback.
5. **§ 9 — No termination for convenience.** No general Customer exit against a three-year term with automatic 12-month renewals. We propose a new § 9.4: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee, and confirmation that Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right; 60 days is available as a fallback.
6. **§ 22.1 — Vendor audit rights.** Audits at any time without notice, plus remote access to our systems. We propose limiting to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, and no system access — which also aligns § 22.1 with § 22.2.
7. **§ 12.4 — One-way non-solicit/no-hire.** 18 months post-termination, covering any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, extending to "engage", with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. We propose deletion, consistent with § 12.3; a narrow mutual version is available as a fallback.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven negotiation items above, with playbook comments stating our position and the offered fallback for each. Deletions (§§ 2.2, 7.2, 12.4) should be framed by reference to §§ 2.1 and 12.3, which already record that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment — these are internal-consistency fixes as much as commercial asks.
2. **Confirm the four non-negotiable positions** in the cover note: deletion of the Customer-payable daily LD (§ 7.6), removal of unannounced audits and remote system access (§ 22.1), a Customer termination-for-convenience right (new § 9.4), and a non-renewal window no longer than 60 days (§ 8.2).
3. **Complete the warranty review.** Manually confirm the § 19.2 Deliverable conformance period and trigger and the § 19.4 remedy language before we close the WARRANTY item; verification did not pass, so we are not recording a conclusion yet. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed pending that check.
4. **Business input on exclusivity (§ 2.2).** Confirm whether any exclusivity is commercially required; if not, we press for straight deletion.
5. **Order Form drafting note to the deal team.** "Deliverable" (§ 1.4) captures only work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, so each Order Form must expressly identify all bespoke work product to secure our § 14.2 ownership.
6. **Retain the favourable provisions** on any counterparty turn: §§ 12.3, 20.1–20.5, 21.1–21.4, 24.1–24.4, 13.1–13.3, 11.1–11.3 and 18.1–18.2 should not be reopened or diluted."}
